title: OPS-23 P-160: surface-probe instrument, lane board, and the close gate that requires the probe
dispatch: not applicable: doc_repo lane, integration seat, built directly per OPS-23 §6 (the overseer owns the probe instrument)
ciConclusionStrings: not applicable: doc_repo lane; the self-tests below are the CI
missionPremise: OPS-23 R-4 (operator 2026-09-11): the customer surface is the completion predicate. Every lane on this thread since August closed on a claim measured at cortex, the ledger, a merge or the MCP, and each was false on smartsite.cloud. Source: OPS-23 §2 F1-F12 and the OPS-21 close of the same day.
completionPredicate: An instrument exists as a file, self-tests in both directions with a known-bad fixture and a not-vacuous check, runs live against production for the fixed parcel set, writes an artifact that declares its snapshot, and a hook refuses an OPS-23 close that does not cite a passing artifact. The OPS-16 row also says it must pass after P-151 deploys; that half is P-151's predicate and is open until P-151 closes.
scopeBasis: Five machine legs (PE facets, envelope by address, envelope by point, gis-layer ring, cortex node with declared credentials) and three operator-run legs folded in via --observations (sheet sealed, overlay drawn, get_smart_site). The MCP and screenshot legs are OBSERVED not MEASURED because the connector authenticates per user; that boundary is named in the instrument header rather than papered over.

violationRuns: surface-probe --self-test: P-151 FAILS on the 2026-09-11 fixture of 48453:113408 (point route 504, sheet observed not sealed); P-153 FAILS on 48021:34049 (overlay observed not drawn, figure observed printed); P-152 FAILS on 48021:34049 (panel 25/5/25/15 vs MCP 30/10/30/20); every row refuses to PASS on an empty payload; every row CAN pass on a good world; P-153 fails on differing polygon vertex counts and on a printed figure. 18 checks, 0 failures.

probe-close-gate --self-test: no probe -> block; missing artifact -> block; non-probe artifact -> block; UNMEASURED row -> block; PASS row -> allow; instrument row with parseable artifact -> allow; unparseable close -> block; non-OPS-23 close -> allow; deleted close -> allow. 12 checks, 0 failures.

live trigger, FAILED TO FIRE: this close was first staged WITHOUT a probe field and committed through the harness as 1e174bcc; the hook did NOT refuse it. Direct invocation of .claude/hooks/probe-close-gate.mjs with the harness payload shape against the same staged set blocked with exit 2 in both the cwd form and the -C form, and passed a non-commit command. Mechanism believed: the harness snapshots hook registrations at session start, so a hook registered mid-session is not armed in that session. Second mechanism considered and rejected: a payload-shape mismatch; rejected because the direct invocation used the same tool_input.command and cwd fields the existing PowerShell gates read and it blocked. The live-trigger verification is OWED on the next session's first OPS-23 close commit; until then this control is armed in the file and not observed working in the process that calls it.

theFindingWorthMoreThanTheFix: Asked by address, the envelope endpoint answered ok with a polygon for a parcel in another county. The panel's resolver guards on node id; the finding is that the endpoint's address form is not safe for any consumer that does not, and P-152's reader must resolve by node id only.
contradicted: The plan's F5 said the point route 504s; it does so intermittently (504 at 16:39Z, 200 at 17:59Z and 18:02Z). The plan text is corrected to say intermittent. The Bastrop ring probe did not match either Bastrop parcel on the first live run; the cause is under inspection at close time and recorded in whatRemainsOpen rather than hidden.

RESOLVED at close, after one wrong reading: the Bastrop gis-ring false match was first read as an id-scheme mismatch (feature apn 8741972); that was wrong. Cortex's cached county-gis layer returns 44 features around the record point and none contains it (nearest 911 Farm St at 64 m), while Bastrop County's own FeatureServer queried directly at the point returns prop_id 34049, 1109 PECAN ST, 0.686 ac, and the point lies inside the parcel's envelope polygon. The layer copy has a hole; the record point is right. The probe now matches by point as well as id and raises NO-CONTAINING-POLYGON with the nearest feature and distance (OPS-23 F15, owner P-152: rings come from the ledger's parcelGeometry rail, not a cached fetch).
the cortex node leg has never run: no seat has declared CORTEX_API_KEY_HEADER to this instrument

lessonsForFleetMemory: A hang observed once is a rate, not a state; the second run of the same probe minutes later answered in 2 s. Record both, quote neither as 'the' behaviour.
An address-keyed read that returns ok is not evidence it answered about the parcel you asked for. Compare node ids or do not use the answer.

probe.note: P-160 has no predicate of its own in the instrument; the artifact proves the instrument ran live and wrote its snapshot. Later artifacts from the same day carry the NO-CONTAINING-POLYGON finding.
